concepts.title: Composition of the Atmosphere
concepts.definition: The atmosphere is a blanket of mixed gases - nitrogen the largest share, oxygen vital for breathing, carbon dioxide small but heat-trapping - along with water vapour and dust; each component plays a role in weather, climate and life.
concepts.key_idea: Nitrogen dominates, oxygen sustains, carbon dioxide warms: every gas has a job.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest103.txt opening sections (composition of the atmosphere)
question_patterns: what is the composition of the atmosphere

solution_steps.explain: Note nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and traces of others.
Breathing, burning, warmth and protection come from different gases.
Water vapour and dust change place to place and drive weather.

concepts.title: Weather and Climate: Elements and Difference
concepts.definition: Weather is the hour-to-hour state of temperature, pressure, wind, humidity, cloud and rainfall, while climate is the long-term average pattern of weather of a place; the two share elements but differ in timescale.
concepts.key_idea: Weather is today's mood, climate is long-term character.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest103.txt sections on weather, climate and their elements
question_patterns: differentiate weather and climate with examples

what does the climate of a place depend on
how is weather recorded and forecast

compare the climates of two regions you know

solution_steps.explain: Weather is short-lived; climate is the long-run pattern.
Temperature, pressure, wind, humidity and rainfall measure both.
Classify given statements as weather or climate.

concepts.title: Climate Change and Its Impacts
concepts.definition: Human activities raise greenhouse gases and warm the planet, shifting rainfall patterns, melting glaciers and raising seas; understanding the atmosphere helps citizens read these changes and support mitigation and adaptation.
concepts.key_idea: The blanket is thickening: climate change rewrites weather patterns worldwide.
concepts.textbook_ref: iest103.txt sections on climate change and impacts
question_patterns: what is climate change and what causes it
how do greenhouse gases warm the earth
list three impacts of climate change on climate patterns
what steps can reduce climate change - suggest mitigation
how can communities adapt to changing climate
connect the greenhouse effect to the given weather event

solution_steps.explain: Burning fuels adds carbon dioxide and Methane to the air.
Trapped heat shifts rainfall, ice and sea levels.
Cutting emissions and adapting practices protect the future.
